mainEntity.name: What should I do first if I want to use AI to build software but have no idea where to start?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Start with a small, clearly defined workflow rather than asking AI to build an entire product. For Run My AI Business readers, that could mean outlining a digital product, drafting a simple website specification, or creating a repeatable research task before attempting custom software.

AI-assisted development can produce useful drafts, explanations, tests, and documentation, but it does not replace product decisions or quality review. Community discussions commonly emphasize writing a specification, splitting work into manageable tasks, and checking every change.

Key factors:
- Define the user, desired outcome, constraints, and edge cases.
- Decide which work requires human judgment.
- Establish tests and approval points before generation.
- Keep credentials and confidential data out of prompts.

Practical guidance: Ask AI to identify missing requirements first, then generate one small component at a time. Run tests, inspect dependencies, and confirm that you understand each material change before using it.

Run My AI Business can help readers understand this focused, human-directed approach through its educational workflows and adaptable assistant examples.
acceptedAnswer.description: Begin with one small, clearly defined workflow. Write down the user, outcome, constraints, and edge cases; ask AI to find gaps; then generate and test one component at a time. Keep human approval before anything is published, connected to accounts, or used in production.
